newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates close steady, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates close steady, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed steady in dull trading on Wednesday, dealers said.

They said the rates were likely to rise in the next few days after officials reduced their 1996/97 (July-June) production estimates to between 9.2 and 9.5 million 375-lb bales from a target of 10 million and compared to 9.6 million in 1995/96.
There was not much immediate reaction to the lower crop forecast, with supplies of cotton to ginneries expected to rise sharply from early November, broker Nasim Usman said.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,000 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), he said.
